clauses.reason: Section 1 added paragraph (o) to Section 1 of Executive Order 10621 (the per diem authority for Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, the Canal Zone and possessions, delegated to the Secretary of Defense). Executive Order 12396 of December 9, 1982, section 5(a), revoked subsections (g), (h), (j), (k), (l), (m) and (n) of Section 1 of EO 10621 but not (o), so section 1 of EO 11294 survived that amendment (later event, no end). Executive Order 12561 of July 1, 1986 revoked subsection (o) in its section 1 and, in section 3, revoked Executive Order No. 11294 of August 4,1966; the express revocation of the order on July 1, 1986 is the first end of this clause.

Section 2 delegated to the Secretary of State the President's authority under section 3 of the Travel Expense Act of 1949 to set maximum per diem rates for areas outside the United States. No instrument is held ending it before Executive Order 12561 of July 1, 1986, whose section 3 revokes Executive Order No. 11294 of August 4,1966, and whose section 2 re-delegates the function to the Secretary of State under the 1985 Act. The first end is that express revocation on July 1, 1986.

Section 3 amended paragraph (9) of Section 1 of Executive Order 11230 (delegation of the per diem authority for travel outside the 48 contiguous States to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget). Executive Order 11609 of July 22, 1971, section 11, lists among the orders hereby superseded Section 3 of Executive Order No. 11294 of August 4, 1966 (and Executive Order 11230 itself), and its section 1 re-delegates the authority; section 12 makes the order effective immediately except paragraphs (1) to (13) and (19) of section 1 (ninety days), and section 11 is not among those paragraphs, so the supersession took effect on the order's date, July 22, 1971. The alternative October 20, 1971 (ninety days after) is the date the replacement paragraphs of section 1 of EO 11609 took effect, not the date section 11 took effect.

Section 4 provides that, to the extent not heretofore superseded, Executive Order No. 10970 of October 27,1961, is superseded. The supersession of EO 10970 took effect on issue on August 4, 1966 and is an accrued effect; as no held source supplies a separate ending event for this sentence as a clause of EO 11294, the clause is recorded as ending with the whole order when Executive Order 12561 of July 1, 1986, section 3, revoked Executive Order No. 11294 of August 4,1966. That choice does not change the whole-order end, which is the same date.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 11294 of August 4, 1966 (31 FR 10601) has four sections, all read in the held Federal Register text: section 1 amends Executive Order 10621 by adding paragraph (o) (the President's authority under section 3 of the Travel Expense Act of 1949 to set maximum per diem rates in Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, the Canal Zone and possessions, delegated to the Secretary of Defense); section 2 delegates to the Secretary of State the same authority for areas outside the United States; section 3 amends paragraph (9) of Section 1 of Executive Order 11230 (the same authority for travel to and between places outside the 48 contiguous States, delegated to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget); and section 4 supersedes Executive Order 10970, to the extent not heretofore superseded. Two later orders act on it. Executive Order 11609 of July 22, 1971, section 11, lists among the orders hereby superseded Section 3 of Executive Order No. 11294 of August 4, 1966 (together with Executive Order 11230 that it amended); section 12 makes the order effective immediately except paragraphs (1) to (13) and (19) of its section 1, so the supersession of section 3 took effect on July 22, 1971 (the machine lead of October 20, 1971 is the ninety-day date for those paragraphs of section 1, which does not include section 11). Executive Order 12561 of July 1, 1986 (51 FR 24299), section 1 revokes subsection (o) of Section 1 of EO 10621 (the paragraph section 1 of EO 11294 added), section 2 re-delegates the per diem authority to the Secretary of State under section 102(a) of the Federal Civilian Employee and Contractor Travel Expenses Act of 1985, and section 3 states that Executive Order No. 11294 of August 4, 1966, is revoked. That express revocation of the whole order on July 1, 1986 ends sections 1, 2 and 4, and is the latest clause end, so the whole order ended on July 1, 1986. Executive Order 12396 of December 9, 1982 revoked subsections (g), (h), (j), (k), (l), (m) and (n) of Section 1 of EO 10621 but not subsection (o), so it did not end section 1. The held U.S. Code note under 3 U.S.C. 301 (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t3-s301.txt) agrees: it says EO 11294, as amended by EO 11609, was revoked by EO 12561. The Federal Register disposition note held for EO 11294 gives EO 10960 of October 27, 1961 as the order superseded, but the order's text (and EO 10970 of October 27, 1961) says 10970; the text controls. The machine lead naming EO 11488 is an unrelated land order that does not cite EO 11294 and is disregarded. Status recommended: no.

savings.reason: The delegated per diem authority did not lapse: Executive Order 12561 of July 1, 1986 re-delegated it in sections 1 and 2 under the 1985 Act, so the function continues under that order's own authority, and the supersession of EO 10970 in section 4 and the earlier amendments of EO 10621 and EO 11230 are accrued effects that no longer depend on EO 11294. EO 11294 contains no savings clause.
